requirements.statement: The view page of a Submitted or Submitted action required notification has a primary 'Amend this notification' button in its header. A Draft or Completed notification's view page has no Amend button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 starts an amendment from the notification itself, where the trader is looking at what was submitted.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Submitted notification's view page has no Amend button: amending starts only from the dashboard card (trace-e2e-p14-050). The backend already allows amending only a SUBMITTED notification (repo-backend-p2-093).

requirements.statement: 'Amend this notification' does not leave the page: it opens a confirmation dialog headed 'Amend notification' (a level-1 heading) that asks 'Are you sure you want to change this notification?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks the trader to confirm before reopening a submitted notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the dashboard card's Amend posts straight away with no confirmation (trace-animals-fit-p3-027).

requirements.statement: The amend dialog's 'Yes, continue' button starts the amendment; its 'No, go back' link-styled button closes the dialog and leaves the trader on the view page, from where 'Amend this notification' can reopen it.
requirements.why: The trader confirms or backs out of amending without losing their place.

requirements.statement: The amend and cancel-amendment dialogs are hidden until opened, are modal dialogs (role dialog, aria-modal) labelled by their heading (the amend dialog also described by its question), and each has a Close (X) button labelled 'Close' for screen readers and an overlay; the Close button, the overlay and the dialog's 'go back' button all dismiss it without acting.
requirements.why: A dialog must be announced and dismissable for keyboard and screen-reader users.

requirements.statement: Confirming an amendment, from the view page or the dashboard card's Amend, takes the trader to the notification's review page (the amend review), not to its overview hub.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 opens an amendment on the review page so the trader sees every answer and its Change link at once.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Amend posts to /notifications/{id}/amend and redirects to the overview hub showing 'Amending' (trace-animals-fit-p3-027, trace-e2e-p14-053, repo-tests-p4-098); the review page is one step further, behind Review and submit (trace-animals-fit-p3-031).

requirements.statement: Amending moves a SUBMITTED notification to AMEND, keeps its reference and original submitted time, stores a full independent snapshot of the submitted content and fulfilments, and records a NotificationAmendmentRequested event carrying the status history and the actor; an unknown reference gets 404 and any status but SUBMITTED gets 400.
requirements.why: The submitted version must survive the amendment so cancelling can restore it and other services see the change.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend amend endpoint already does this (repo-backend-p2-090, repo-backend-p2-094, repo-backend-p2-098), proven end to end (trace-e2e-p14-070).

requirements.statement: Answers changed during an amendment are saved to the notification record (status stays AMEND) as the trader goes, and are not visible as the submitted version until resubmitted.
requirements.why: The real service persists every save; the prototype's session-only amendment cannot express persistence.
requirements.deltaNote: Saving keeps a notification in AMEND (repo-backend-p2-111), and a changed value survives leaving the cancel page (trace-animals-fit-p3-042).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended shows the status tag 'Amend'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the state 'Amend'.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the tag reads 'Amending' (yellow) on the hub, review and cancel pages (trace-animals-fit-p3-029, trace-e2e-p14-031).

requirements.statement: During an amendment, the review page and every question page show an Amend status bar above the caption and heading: the 'Amend' tag, the reference, and a link-styled 'Cancel amend' button that opens the cancel-amendment dialog.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader abandon the amendment from wherever they are in it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a 'Cancel amendment' link sits under the review page heading only; the hub and question pages offer no way to cancel (trace-animals-fit-p3-032, trace-animals-fit-p3-029-m1, trace-e2e-p14-055).

requirements.statement: The amend review ends with three actions: 'Continue' (submits), a secondary 'Cancel amend' button that opens the cancel-amendment dialog, and a red 'Delete' button linking to the delete confirmation.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts every way out of an amendment at the foot of the review.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the amending review ends with Continue only and offers neither Delete nor a Cancel button there (trace-e2e-p14-032, trace-e2e-p14-032-m1).

requirements.statement: The amend review is headed and titled 'Review your notification' when first opened, and 'Review before re-submitting' once any answer differs from the submitted version; only notification answers count as a change.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells the trader they are about to resubmit something changed.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the amending review is always headed 'Review your notification' (trace-animals-fit-p3-032, repo-tests-p3-086).

requirements.statement: The amend review has no page-header actions (no Amend this notification, no Copy as new), no Import reference numbers section and no Date submitted line.
requirements.why: During an amendment the status bar replaces the view page's header.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's amending view shows no Copy as new or Delete under its heading (trace-e2e-p14-032-m1) and has no Import reference numbers section or Date submitted line.

requirements.statement: The amend review is editable, with a Change link on every card (the first going to the origin of the import), and its Back link goes to the notification's overview hub.
requirements.why: Amending means changing the submitted answers.
requirements.deltaNote: The amending review already has Change links on every card and a Back link to the hub (trace-e2e-p14-032, trace-animals-fit-p3-034).

requirements.statement: A question page opened from the amend review offers three actions: 'Save and return' (back to the amend review, which shows the changed answer), a secondary 'Save and continue', and a link-styled 'Save and return to overview'; the posted action values are review, continue and hub. Pages reached from another page rather than from the overview keep the primary button alone, as DR1 ruled (inc-161).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader return to the review straight after a change, or carry on.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Change link opens the question with ?change=1 and saving returns to the notification view with no choice of where to go (trace-e2e-p14-047, repo-tests-p3-079).

requirements.statement: During an amendment, question pages keep the journey's usual Back links (the origin of the import back to the notification type page, arrival details back to the overview hub), not a link to the amend review.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not change Back links for an amendment.

requirements.statement: During an amendment, question pages are prefilled with the notification's saved answers and keep their usual copy (for example Arrival details: arrival date at port of entry with a d/m/yyyy date picker, port of entry search, means of transport, transport identification and document reference).
requirements.why: The trader changes only what needs changing.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Change link during an amendment opens the question with the saved answers (repo-tests-p3-079, trace-e2e-p14-046).

requirements.statement: Continue on the amend review does not go on while an answer is invalid or incomplete (such as an arrival date outside 7 days back to 6 months ahead).
requirements.why: A resubmitted amendment must be complete and valid.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an amendment reaches the declaration only once every task row is fulfilled (repo-tests-p3-085); whether the trader is told why is the question.

requirements.statement: Continue on a valid amend review goes to the Declaration page; ticking the declaration and pressing Continue resubmits the amendment.
requirements.why: An amendment is resubmitted through the same declaration as a first submission.
requirements.deltaNote: Continue on the amending review already leads to the Declaration, and ticking it resubmits (repo-tests-p3-088, repo-tests-p3-091, trace-e2e-p14-056).

requirements.statement: The Declaration page at the end of an amendment shows no Amend status bar, and its Back link goes to the review page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the same Declaration page as a first submission.

requirements.statement: Resubmitting an amendment shows the ordinary 'Import notification submitted' confirmation with the notification's existing reference and no wording about an amendment; the same record becomes Submitted again, read only, with the edited answers, the dashboard shows the amended answers, and it can be amended again.
requirements.why: An amendment replaces the submitted notification rather than creating a second one.
requirements.deltaNote: Resubmission already lands on the submitted confirmation and the notification is Submitted, read only and amendable again with the edited value (repo-tests-p3-092, trace-e2e-p14-057, trace-e2e-p14-059).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment dialog is headed 'Are you sure you want to cancel this amendment?' as a level-2 heading, with no description line.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording for cancelling an amendment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the cancel-amend page's title and level-1 heading are 'Cancel this amendment?' (repo-frontend-p3-080, trace-e2e-p14-035).

requirements.statement: Cancelling an amendment shows no paragraph explaining that changes will be discarded and the submitted version restored.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's cancel-amendment dialog has no description line.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page says 'Your changes since you started amending will be discarded and the submitted version restored.' (repo-frontend-p3-081, trace-e2e-p14-036).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirm button reads 'Yes, cancel amendment' and is a standard (not warning) primary button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on this button.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's cancel-amend page already has a standard 'Yes, cancel amendment' button (repo-frontend-p3-082, trace-animals-fit-p3-038).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment dialog's way back is a link-styled 'Go back' button that closes the dialog and leaves the amendment in progress, replacing the secondary button 'No, return to notification'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording and pattern for not cancelling.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the way back is a secondary button-styled link 'No, return to notification' to the notification view (repo-frontend-p3-083, trace-e2e-p14-039).

requirements.statement: 'Cancel amend' opens the cancel-amendment confirmation as a dialog over the current page rather than navigating to a separate page with a journey strip and Back link; without script, the same control reaches a confirmation page carrying only the dialog's heading and buttons.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 confirms cancellation in place; a no-script route keeps the action usable for everyone.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Cancel amendment' navigates to a page at /notifications/{id}/cancel-amend with the Amending journey strip and a Back link to the notification view (repo-frontend-p3-078, trace-e2e-p14-034, trace-e2e-p14-037).

requirements.statement: Confirming the cancellation discards every edit made during the amendment, restores the submitted content and fulfilments, returns the notification to SUBMITTED with its original submitted time, records one NotificationAmendmentCancelled event, and takes the trader to that notification's view page, read only and showing Submitted.
requirements.why: Cancelling must leave the notification exactly as it was submitted.
requirements.deltaNote: Cancel-amend already restores the snapshot and returns to the read-only Submitted view (repo-backend-p2-105, trace-e2e-p14-045, trace-animals-fit-p3-047).

requirements.statement: After an amendment is cancelled, the view page shows no success banner and its address carries no ?cancelled=1.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns to the view page without a message.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the view opens at ?cancelled=1 with a 'Success' banner reading 'The amendment has been cancelled and the submitted version restored.' (trace-animals-fit-p3-044, trace-animals-fit-p3-045, repo-tests-p3-080).

requirements.statement: Opening or posting cancel amendment for a notification that is not being amended changes nothing and returns the trader to the overall dashboard with no message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route silently.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Submitted notification is redirected to its view page, and any other status to the live-animals dashboard (repo-frontend-p3-079, repo-frontend-p3-087).

requirements.statement: When copy as new, cancel amendment or delete fails to save, the page the trader came from is shown again with HTTP 500 and the recoverable-error banner.
requirements.why: A real save can fail; the prototype cannot express that.
requirements.deltaNote: Each controller already re-renders with 500 and the recoverable-error banner (repo-frontend-p3-076, repo-frontend-p3-088, repo-frontend-p3-102).

requirements.statement: Every notification's view page header offers 'Copy as new': Submitted, Submitted action required, Completed and Draft alike.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader start a new notification from any existing one.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Submitted view offers Copy as new but a Draft view has none (trace-e2e-p14-049, trace-e2e-p14-051).

requirements.statement: On the view page, 'Copy as new' is a secondary button when 'Amend this notification' sits beside it, and the primary button when it does not (Draft, Completed).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps one primary action per header.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Copy as new on the view page is always secondary (trace-e2e-p14-049).

requirements.statement: Copy as new goes straight, with no confirmation, to the new draft's overview hub titled 'Overview', which has no Back link and no banner announcing the copy.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree that copying is immediate and quiet.
requirements.deltaNote: Copy already redirects straight to the new notification's overview with no banner (trace-e2e-p3-073, trace-e2e-p3-077, trace-animals-fit-p2-075).

requirements.statement: A copy is a new notification saved at once as a Draft, with its own new reference (same GBN-AG prefix, fresh suffix); the source is unchanged, the copy is independent of it, every copy is distinct, and a NotificationCreated event (carrying the acting user's organisation id to resolve address-book parties) is recorded for the copy only.
requirements.why: Copying must never alter or merge with the notification it came from.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy endpoint already makes a new DRAFT with a new reference and leaves the source alone (repo-backend-p2-042, repo-backend-p2-044, trace-e2e-p14-074).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the origin of the import: country of origin, whether a region of origin code is required, and the region of origin code with its suffix.
requirements.why: These describe the trade, not the shipment, so they usually repeat.
requirements.deltaNote: The copy mapper keeps them (repo-backend-p2-047) and the copy's origin page comes back prefilled (trace-animals-fit-p2-078).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the internal reference number, in the notification record as well as on the page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 carries it over with the import details.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy mapper clears the internal reference in the notification record (repo-backend-p2-048), though the copy's origin page shows it from the copied fulfilments (trace-animals-fit-p2-078).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over what is being imported: the commodity (id, code and name), the commodity selections, the selected species and the notification type (worked out from the copied answers when missing).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks What are you importing? Complete on the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy mapper keeps the commodity name and each complement's type but clears every complement's species list (repo-backend-p2-049, repo-backend-p2-050, repo-backend-p2-051).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the number of animals, the number of packages or the net weight: the copy's commodity details show To do, its Animals total reads 0 and its Packages/boxes total shows no figure.
requirements.why: Counts are specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's overview carries the totals (1 animal, 5 packages) and marks Commodity details Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109, trace-animals-fit-p2-077), though the copy mapper clears them in the record (repo-backend-p2-051).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over animal identifiers (ear tags, passports and the like): the copy's Identification details show To do.
requirements.why: Identifiers belong to the animals in one shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Identification details show Complete (trace-e2e-p13-109, trace-e2e-p3-075), though the copy mapper drops identifiers from the record (repo-backend-p2-052).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the main reason for import and its follow-ups: internal market purpose, transhipment destination country, transit exit border control post, transit destination country, and the temporary admission exit date and port of exit.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks Main import reason Complete on the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy mapper keeps the reason, purpose, destination country and port of exit but clears the exit date (repo-backend-p2-053, repo-backend-p2-059, repo-backend-p2-062).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the additional animal details: what the animals are certified for, whether unweaned animals are included, and the storage temperature.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks Additional details Complete on the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy mapper keeps certified-for but clears the unweaned animals answer (repo-backend-p2-054).

requirements.statement: When copying, a certified-for value that is no longer an option is mapped to a current one: 'Breeding' and 'Breeding and/or production' become 'Further keeping', 'Slaughter' stays 'Slaughter', and any other value not offered becomes 'Further keeping'.
requirements.why: A copy must not carry an answer the trader can no longer choose.

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the roles and addresses (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination, each in full as stored), the CPH number and the permanent address details.
requirements.why: Trading partners usually repeat between shipments.
requirements.deltaNote: The copy mapper keeps every party, the CPH number and the whole fulfilments payload (repo-backend-p2-055, repo-backend-p2-058, repo-backend-p2-063).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the arrival details (port of entry, arrival date, means of transport, transport identification and transport document reference): the copy's Arrival details show To do.
requirements.why: Arrival is specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Arrival details show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109), though the copy mapper clears the transport block in the record (repo-backend-p2-060).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the transit countries.
requirements.why: The route is specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Transit countries show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the transporter: the copy's Transport details show To do.
requirements.why: The transporter is chosen per shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Transport details show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the contact address: the copy's Contact address shows To do.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for the contact address again on each notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Contact address shows Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-animals-fit-p2-077), though the copy mapper clears the consignment block in the record (repo-backend-p2-061).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over uploaded documents: the copy's Upload documents shows To do.
requirements.why: Documents are specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Upload documents already shows To do on a copy (trace-e2e-p3-076).

requirements.statement: Copying a notification that is being amended copies its submitted version, not the edits in progress.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copies the saved notification; an unfinished amendment is not yet the notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today copying an AMEND notification copies its current, edited content (repo-backend-p2-066).

requirements.statement: Copy as new for a notification the trader cannot reach (unknown reference, or a status that cannot be copied such as deleted) changes nothing and returns to the overall dashboard with no message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route silently.
requirements.deltaNote: Copy already returns an unknown notification to the dashboard with no banner (repo-frontend-p3-073); the backend refuses unknown (404) and uncopyable (400) sources (repo-backend-p2-037, repo-backend-p2-038). Which dashboard is req for c-manage-notifications-010.

requirements.statement: Copy as new is checked against the version the trader was looking at: if the notification changed since, nothing is copied and the trader returns to where they started (the dashboard or the notification's view page) with the 'The notification has been updated' banner. A stale copy from the view page must land on the view page, not on a missing check-answers page.
requirements.why: A trader must never copy content different from what they saw; the prototype cannot express concurrent edits.
requirements.deltaNote: The token check and banner exist (repo-frontend-p3-074, repo-backend-p2-040), but a stale copy started from the view page redirects to /notifications/{id}/check-answers?staleAction=1, which no route serves (repo-frontend-p3-075-m1).

requirements.statement: Every notification's view page header offers a red 'Delete' warning button linking to the delete confirmation: Submitted, Submitted action required, Completed and Draft alike.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader delete any notification from the notification itself.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Submitted view offers Delete but a Draft view does not (trace-e2e-p14-049, trace-e2e-p14-051).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended can be deleted (from the amend review's Delete button), and the backend's soft-delete API description says DRAFT, SUBMITTED and AMEND notifications can be deleted.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers Delete during an amendment, and the API must describe what it does.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend and frontend already delete AMEND notifications (repo-backend-p3-034, repo-frontend-p3-091), but the API description says only DRAFT and SUBMITTED (repo-backend-p3-035) and no fit spec proves deleting an amending notification (repo-frontend-p3-135-m1).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page identifies the notification in a GOV.UK summary list with the rows 'Reference number', 'Commodity', 'Number' and 'Origin' (the country of origin).
requirements.why: The trader confirms they are deleting the right notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete page has only a heading, one sentence and two buttons (repo-frontend-p3-092, repo-frontend-p3-093).

requirements.statement: The delete page's Commodity row lists each commodity's common name with its species' Latin names in brackets, comma-separated (for example 'Sheep (Ovis Aries), Goat (Capra Hircus)'); for other live mammals each species' common name is used.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's format for naming what was notified.

requirements.statement: The delete page's Number row shows the total number of packages for a germinal-products-only notification, and otherwise the total number of animals.
requirements.why: Germinal products are counted in packages, animals by head.

requirements.statement: A delete page summary row with no value from the notification falls back to what the dashboard lists for it, and shows 'Not applicable' when that is empty too.
requirements.why: Every row shows something, even for an early draft.

requirements.statement: Below the summary the delete page says 'Confirm that you want to delete this notification.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's confirmation wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page has no such sentence (repo-frontend-p3-093).

requirements.statement: The delete page warns 'This action cannot be undone.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's warning wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today it reads 'This cannot be undone.' (repo-frontend-p3-093, trace-e2e-p3-060).

requirements.statement: The delete page's red warning button reads 'Yes, delete'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's button wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today it reads 'Yes, delete notification' (repo-frontend-p3-095, trace-animals-fit-p3-008).

requirements.statement: Beside 'Yes, delete' the delete page has a plain link 'No, cancel' in the button group, replacing the secondary button 'No, return to dashboard'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording and pattern for not deleting.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the way back is a secondary button-styled link 'No, return to dashboard' (repo-frontend-p3-096, trace-animals-fit-p3-009).

requirements.statement: The delete page's Back link and 'No, cancel' both return to the notification's view page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the trader back to the notification they were deleting.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both go to the dashboard (repo-frontend-p3-097, trace-animals-fit-p3-010, trace-e2e-p3-063).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page shows no journey strip (status tag and reference) above its heading; the summary list identifies the notification instead.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 builds the page from GOV.UK components only.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page shows the journey strip with the status tag and reference (repo-frontend-p3-094-m1, trace-e2e-p3-064).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page is titled 'Delete this notification? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' with the level-1 heading 'Delete this notification?', serves every deletable status, and can be opened directly by its address.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the heading.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's delete page already has this title and heading for drafts and submitted notifications (trace-animals-fit-p3-006-m1, trace-animals-fit-p3-013).

requirements.statement: Confirming the delete (a POST with the CSRF crumb) soft-deletes the notification: its status becomes DELETED and the record is kept; a repeat is a harmless no-op; a NotificationDeleted (draft) or NotificationSubmissionDeleted (submitted or amending) event is recorded with the actor and organisation id; an unknown reference gets 404.
requirements.why: The real store keeps deleted records for other services and audit; the prototype's outright removal cannot express persistence.
requirements.deltaNote: Delete already soft-deletes through the backend, idempotently, with the events (repo-backend-p3-033, repo-backend-p3-036, repo-backend-p3-040, trace-e2e-p14-078).

requirements.statement: After 'Yes, delete' the trader lands on the overall dashboard, which shows no banner.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns to the service's front page after a delete.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the trader lands on the live-animals dashboard at /live-animals?deleted=1 with a banner (repo-frontend-p3-099, trace-e2e-p3-066).

requirements.statement: The deletion success message reads '<reference> has been deleted' (or 'Notification has been deleted' when the reference is not known), and appears on the live-animals notification list the next time the trader opens it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the deleted notification where the trader looks for it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner reads 'The notification has been deleted.' straight after the delete (trace-animals-fit-p3-018, trace-e2e-p3-068).

requirements.statement: The deletion message is a GOV.UK success notification banner with role alert, titled 'Success'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's banner title.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner is titled 'Notification deleted' (trace-animals-fit-p3-017, trace-e2e-p3-067).

requirements.statement: The deletion message is held for the trader and shown once, not driven by a ?deleted=1 query string.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 carries the message to the next visit of the list.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner depends on ?deleted=1 in the address (trace-e2e-p3-070).

requirements.statement: The deletion success banner dismisses itself after 5 seconds.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sets the banner to auto-dismiss.

requirements.statement: A deleted notification no longer appears in the notification list, and searching for its reference finds nothing.
requirements.why: Deleted notifications are gone from the trader's view.
requirements.deltaNote: The deleted notification already disappears from the dashboard and its search (trace-animals-fit-p3-020, trace-e2e-p3-072).

requirements.statement: Opening or posting delete for a notification the trader cannot reach (unknown reference, or a status that cannot be deleted) changes nothing and returns to the overall dashboard with no message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route; the real service must also check the record exists, which the prototype's POST does not.
requirements.deltaNote: Delete already refuses an unknown or non-deletable notification and returns to the dashboard with no banner (repo-frontend-p3-100, repo-frontend-p3-101); which dashboard follows c-manage-notifications-010.

requirements.statement: The notification view page's level-1 heading is the notification reference, and its browser title is the service name alone ('Import notification service - GOV.UK').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 identifies the page by the notification itself.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the view page's heading is 'Review your notification', at the notification's notification-view path (repo-tests-p3-072).

requirements.statement: Beside the reference heading the view page shows the status as a tag: 'Draft', 'Submitted', 'Completed', or 'Submitted action required' when conditional submission items are outstanding.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts the status with the reference in the page header.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the status tag and reference sit in a journey strip above a 'Review your notification' heading, and only Draft, Submitted and Amending exist (repo-tests-p3-073, trace-animals-fit-p3-046).

requirements.statement: Under its header the view page shows 'Date submitted: <date>' for a submitted or completed notification and 'Date created: <date>' for a draft.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 dates every notification.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend records submittedAt (repo-backend-p2-098), but no page shows it today (trace-e2e-p14-062).

requirements.statement: A Submitted action required notification's header shows a GOV.UK warning text saying what the trader must do (for example 'You need to upload a health certificate').
requirements.why: The trader sees at once why the notification needs action.

requirements.statement: The view page shows an 'Import reference numbers' section in every state, Draft included, warning 'You must use the correct reference and code on the customs declaration or your consignment will be delayed.'
requirements.why: The trader needs these numbers for the customs declaration.

requirements.statement: The Import reference numbers section shows the 'Notification reference' and the 'Customs document code' (C640 for live animals).
requirements.why: Both go on the customs declaration.

requirements.statement: Each import reference row has its own secondary 'Copy' button that copies that row's value.
requirements.why: Saves retyping a reference into the customs declaration.

requirements.statement: The view page shows the notification's answers in the same six numbered sections and cards as the review page (1. About the consignment to 6. Contact address); the card contents follow the review page's requirements.
requirements.why: One rendering of a notification's answers serves review and view.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's notification view already renders the review page's six numbered sections (trace-animals-fit-p3-051); differences inside the cards are carried by the review page's requirements.

requirements.statement: A Submitted, Completed or Submitted action required notification's view page is read only (no Change links); a Submitted or Completed one ends after section 6 with no Continue button.
requirements.why: A submitted notification is changed only through an amendment.
requirements.deltaNote: The Submitted view is already read only with no Continue (trace-e2e-p14-048, repo-tests-p3-070).

requirements.statement: A Submitted action required notification's view page ends with a 'Continue' link to the notification's overview hub.
requirements.why: The trader goes on to supply what is outstanding.

requirements.statement: On a Submitted action required notification's view page, each section missing information shows an inline section error instead of its content ('Enter a minimum of 1 identifier' under Identification details, 'Upload a valid health certificate' in section 4), without an error summary.
requirements.why: The trader sees exactly what is outstanding.

requirements.statement: The view page's Back link goes to the overall dashboard for every status, Draft included.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns from a notification to where the trader found it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the view page's Back link goes to the notification's overview hub (trace-e2e-p14-052, trace-animals-fit-p3-050).

requirements.statement: A Draft notification's view page is editable: every card has a Change link to its question page, and it ends with a Continue button.
requirements.why: A draft can still be changed before submitting.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's Draft view already shows Change links and ends with Continue (trace-e2e-p14-051).

requirements.statement: A Draft notification's view page lists its incomplete sections in a GOV.UK error summary headed 'There is a problem', each item linking to its card, and each incomplete card shows a GOV.UK error message under its heading.
requirements.why: The trader sees what is left to do before submitting.

requirements.statement: Dashboard notification cards keep their status-driven actions: Draft offers Resume, Copy as new and Delete; Submitted offers View, Amend, Copy as new and Delete; Amending offers Resume, Copy as new, Cancel amendment and Delete, each with the reference in its visually hidden accessible name.
requirements.why: DR1 ruled (inc-030) to keep the card's status-driven links rather than flatten them to Copy as new and View.
requirements.deltaNote: The dashboard cards already offer these actions by status (trace-e2e-p14-060).

requirements.statement: The backend notification API supports the lifecycle: create gives DRAFT with a minted reference; save keeps DRAFT or AMEND; submit takes DRAFT or AMEND to SUBMITTED and stamps submittedAt; amend takes SUBMITTED to AMEND; cancel-amend takes AMEND back to SUBMITTED; copy reads DRAFT, SUBMITTED or AMEND and makes a new DRAFT; soft-delete makes DELETED. Each write advances the concurrency token, takes an optional actor, and callers from outside carry the API key.
requirements.why: Every action in this area rests on these transitions.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend already implements this lifecycle (repo-backend-p2-111), proven through the API (trace-e2e-p14-067, trace-e2e-p14-070, trace-e2e-p14-077).

requirements.statement: A notification is saved as a draft as the trader goes: one record per reference, keeping its created date, without errors or transient page state.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 autosaves drafts; the real service persists each save.
requirements.deltaNote: Each journey page's save already persists the whole record under its reference (repo-tests-p4-095, repo-tests-p4-096, trace-e2e-p14-083).

requirements.statement: The delete and cancel-amendment confirmations, the restored submitted view and a copied notification's overview have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations.
requirements.why: The service must meet accessibility standards.
requirements.deltaNote: The fit specs already assert this (repo-frontend-p3-123, repo-frontend-p3-127, repo-frontend-p3-132).

requirements.statement: The tests repo's animals specs and page objects for amend, cancel amendment, copy as new and delete assert the Design Release 2.1 behaviour (new copy, dialogs, landing pages and banners), keep the smoke-tagged cancel and delete cases, and cover what today goes unproven: deleting an amending notification and the guard redirects.
requirements.why: End-to-end proof must follow the changed behaviour.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's specs assert the current copy ('Yes, delete notification', 'Cancel this amendment?', 'Amending', ?deleted=1, ?cancelled=1) and do not prove a way back from delete (repo-tests-p3-095, repo-tests-p3-075, repo-tests-p3-099).

requirements.statement: Every new or changed string on the delete and cancel-amendment confirmations, the amend dialog and the view page has a Welsh entry.
requirements.why: Today's action pages carry Welsh copy, which Design Release 2.1 does not show at all.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete and cancel-amend pages have machine-drafted Welsh copy for their current strings (repo-frontend-p3-089, repo-frontend-p3-104).

requirements.statement: Delete and cancel amendment are checked against the version the trader opened, and the dashboard Amend carries a concurrency token.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: delete and cancel-amend post a token nobody reads, and Amend posts none. Design Release 2.1 does not ask for a fix, so the programme does not make one.

requirements.statement: Soft delete checks that the caller owns the notification or is an admin.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report as an access-control weakness in the backend; Design Release 2.1 does not cover it, so it needs its own ticket.

requirements.statement: Create, save, copy, submit, amend and cancel-amend write audit records attributed to a user.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: only deletes and replays are audited, and the write endpoints take no user id. Design Release 2.1 does not ask for audit.

requirements.statement: Backend edge cases answer with a client error rather than a server error: copy with a missing token or no content, amend with no fulfilments, a second submit or amend inside the outbox lock window, and submit of an empty notification.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report as backend defects no user journey reaches; Design Release 2.1 does not cover them.

requirements.statement: The place of destination picker's search does not fail with HTTP 500, and the 500 page offers a way back.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: seen on the copy test's first attempt, it belongs to the address pickers and the error page, not to copying.

requirements.statement: The prototype's own mechanics are reproduced: its session keys and journey resets, page modifier classes, ?reference addressing, seeded review snapshots and their fixed sample data.
requirements.why: Prototype internals with nothing a user sees; the real service persists notifications in the backend and has its own test data.

requirements.statement: Amend for a notification the trader cannot amend (unknown reference, or not Submitted) changes nothing and returns to the overall dashboard with no message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the amend route silently.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend refuses an unknown (404) or non-SUBMITTED (400) amend (repo-backend-p2-092, repo-backend-p2-093); no frontend evidence shows what the trader sees.

conflicts.about: Whether amend, cancel amendment and copy as new are started by links (GET) as the prototype draws them, or by form posts.

positions.says: The amend and cancel-amendment dialogs' confirm buttons and Copy as new are links to GET routes that change state.
State-changing actions are form posts carrying the CSRF crumb (and the concurrency token).
A real constraint the prototype cannot express (validation, authentication) overrides it.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: a state change is a POST with the CSRF crumb, an authentication constraint the prototype cannot express. Each control looks and reads as Design Release 2.1 draws it (a button, a link-styled button) but submits a form. The prototype's claim is kept for where each control leads.

conflicts.about: Amend and cancel-amendment confirmations: a custom modal dialog (Design Release 2.1) or a separate confirmation page (today's cancel-amend).

positions.says: Both confirmations are modal dialogs opened over the review or view page.
The dialog is a custom component; GOV.UK Frontend has no modal, and a confirmation page would keep to the toolbox.
Cancel amendment is a separate GET/POST page at /notifications/{id}/cancel-amend.
The prototype wins by default over what the real services do today.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins: build the dialogs as drawn. No DR1 judgement covers them, and keeping to GOV.UK components is house practice, not one of the ruling's overrides. Because the action must work as a form post (c-manage-notifications-001), each trigger also works without script: it reaches a confirmation page at today's route with the dialog's heading and buttons. Today's page claim is kept as the evidence for that route.

conflicts.about: Where confirming an amendment lands: the review page (Design Release 2.1) or the overview hub (today).

positions.says: After choosing to amend, the trader goes to the notification's review page.
Amend posts and lands on the notification's hub.
Amend redirects to the notification's task list hub.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks the tests repo and today's traces: amending lands on the amend review. The tests and trace claims stay as the evidence of today's behaviour.

conflicts.about: Whether edits during an amendment are saved to the record, or held only in the session as the prototype does.

positions.says: Nothing is saved automatically while amending, and cancelling leaves edits in the session without writing them back.
Save keeps a notification in AMEND and persists it, with the submitted version held as a snapshot.
A persistence constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the real service keeps saving amendment edits to the AMEND record behind the submitted snapshot. What the trader sees is the same as Design Release 2.1. The prototype claim is not overruled because it also backs draft autosave (req for drafts).

conflicts.about: Whether delete removes the notification (prototype) or soft-deletes it (today).

positions.says: Confirming the delete removes the notification.
Soft delete keeps the record and its content and sets the status to DELETED, publishing an event.
Persistence and cross-service constraints the prototype cannot express override it.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: delete stays a soft delete with its events. To the trader it looks the same as the prototype's removal.

conflicts.about: Dashboard card actions: Copy as new and View only (Design Release 2.1's list) or the status-driven set (today).

positions.says: inc-030 rejected: keep the card's status-driven links; do not flatten to Copy as new and View.
A live-animals dashboard row offers Copy as new and View.
Cards show Resume, View, Amend, Copy as new, Cancel amendment and Delete by status.

conflicts.outcome: The DR1 judgement on this same difference outranks the prototype: the cards keep their status-driven actions. The prototype claim is not overruled because it also shows a deleted notification gone from the list.

conflicts.about: Whether DR1's inc-026 (treat the delete and cancel-amend pages as unassessed, raise nothing about their copy) stops the Design Release 2.1 copy changes.

positions.says: Delete and amend may be capabilities DR1 did not draw, so the pages need reviewing against DR2 designs, not DR1.
Until the designer settles scope, raise nothing about the pages' copy, buttons or wording.
The delete page is headed 'Delete this notification?' with Design Release 2.1's summary, wording and buttons.

conflicts.outcome: DR1 ranks above the prototype, and its judgement confines itself to the DR1 comparison and sends these pages to a DR2 comparison. Design Release 2.1 is that comparison, so its copy is adopted. Nothing is overruled.

conflicts.about: What a copy carries over: Design Release 2.1's list, the backend copy mapper's list, or everything but documents (what today's pages show).

positions.says: Copy carries import details, what is imported, reasons, additional details, parties and CPH, and clears counts, identifiers, arrival, transit, transporter, documents and contact address.
Copy keeps identification, commodity type and addresses, and resets logistics and per-animal counts, also clearing the internal reference, species, unweaned answer and exit date.
Today a copy's overview shows every task Complete except Upload documents.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks both: a copy carries exactly Design Release 2.1's list, in the record and on the pages alike. Each field that differs is its own requirement. The backend and trace claims stay as evidence of today's behaviour.

conflicts.about: Copying a notification mid-amendment: the submitted version (prototype) or the edits in progress (today).

positions.says: Copy by reference uses the notification's saved snapshot, which an unfinished amendment does not change.
Copying an AMEND notification copies its current, edited content.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks the backend: copy the submitted version. The backend already holds it as the amend snapshot, so no constraint stands in the way.

conflicts.about: Which dashboard the guards, delete and the view page's Back link return to: the overall dashboard (Design Release 2.1) or the live-animals dashboard and hub (today).

positions.says: After a delete the trader lands on the overall dashboard (titled Dashboard, h1 Import notification service); the guards and the view page's Back link go there too.
The dashboard is temporary in the animals frontend and moves to trade-imports-ins-frontend.
Delete returns to the live-animals dashboard at /live-animals?deleted=1.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks today's frontend: these routes return to the overall dashboard, which in the real services is the INS front door's dashboard, where DR1's notes say the dashboard belongs. The live-animals list shows the deletion message on its next visit.

conflicts.about: Whether today's Welsh copy on the action pages is kept and extended, when Design Release 2.1 shows no Welsh at all.

positions.says: The cancel-amend and delete pages have machine-drafted Welsh copy.
The ruling does not say whether something a real service has and Design Release 2.1 does not show at all is removed or left alone.

conflicts.outcome: Neither precedence nor the ruling settles a feature Design Release 2.1 is silent on.
conflicts.question: Should the action pages keep Welsh copy, with Welsh entries added for every string Design Release 2.1 changes or adds?
conflicts.default: Keep Welsh: every changed or new string gets a Welsh entry, marked as a machine draft awaiting a translator, as today's are.

conflicts.about: Whether the deletion success banner dismisses itself after 5 seconds, as Design Release 2.1 sets it.

positions.says: The deletion banner is set to dismiss itself after 5 seconds.
Today's deletion banner is a GOV.UK success banner with role alert that stays on the page.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default, but a message that vanishes after 5 seconds can fail WCAG 2.2.1 (timing adjustable), and the ruling does not say whether an accessibility requirement counts as a real constraint.
conflicts.question: Should the deletion banner disappear by itself after 5 seconds, as Design Release 2.1 sets it, despite the accessibility risk?
conflicts.default: No auto-dismiss: the banner stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page; everything else about it follows Design Release 2.1.

conflicts.about: What the trader sees when Continue on the amend review is refused because an answer is invalid: nothing (the amend trace) or the error summary the draft review shows.

positions.says: Continue on the amend review is silently held: the same page comes back with no error summary or message.
A draft's review lists incomplete sections in a GOV.UK error summary, each linking to its card.
An amendment can only be resubmitted once every task row is fulfilled.

conflicts.outcome: Design Release 2.1 contradicts itself between its draft and amend reviews, and precedence cannot settle a disagreement within one source.
conflicts.question: When Continue on the amend review is refused, should the trader see the same error summary and card error messages as on a draft's review, or stay on the page with no message as the amend trace shows?
conflicts.default: Hold Continue and show the draft review's error summary and card error messages for each invalid or incomplete section.
